title: The garden and the names (Genesis 2:8–20)
hookLine: the human is set in a garden to tend it, and names the animals

lines: A GARDEN, PLANTED IN THE EAST.
A RIVER STILL ON THE MAP.
cards: What was Adam's first job? Before any fruit, any serpent, any fall, Genesis gives the first human work. Not a throne.
A garden. Somewhere in the east, the story says, God plants it, with every tree pleasant to look at and good for food, and a river running out of it that splits into four.
One, the Euphrates, is still on the map today, and another, Hiddekel, is usually taken to be the Tigris. And the first person in the Bible is put to work as a gardener, and asked to name the animals.

teach.b: The garden's name is Eden. In Hebrew it sounds like a word for delight, or luxury. When the Bible was put into Greek, the translators called this garden a paradeisos, a word for a park.

teach.h: TO DRESS IT AND TO KEEP IT.
teach.b: But the verse that matters most today is fifteen, in the King James Bible: "And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it." Two Hebrew verbs.

The first, avad, means to work, to serve; it's the word used later for serving God in worship. The second, shamar, means to keep, to guard, to watch over; the same word is used later for keeping God's commandments.
So the first human job is to serve the ground and guard it.
Christians have read this verse in different ways over the centuries, some stressing the human as ruler of creation, others, more recently, the human as caretaker.
Then God brings every animal to the man, "to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof." God doesn't hand out a list.

teach.h: GOD WAITS TO SEE THE NAMES.
teach.b: God waits to see. Naming, in this story, is how a human pays attention.
And so ends a week that began on a lookout and went back to the very beginning: light, good, image, dust and breath, and now a garden to tend.

how: Some Christians read Genesis 2:15 as a call to care for creation, and churches of several traditions hold creation-care services, community gardens and blessings of animals.

games.q: what's inside the garden — tap the pairs.
p: Greek: a park, our word paradise

s: the first human's first job, before the fall, was work in a garden
"to dress it and to keep it."
God hands Adam a list of the animals' names
God brings them "to see what he would call them." the names are Adam's.
none of Eden's rivers has a name we still use
one is the Euphrates; another, Hiddekel, is usually taken to be the Tigris.

games.q: you're the first human, alone in a new garden. God brings every animal in front of you. what happens next?
o: you give each one a name, and God waits to see what you'll call them.
you choose one to rule the others.
games.why: "whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof." God waits to see. naming is how a human pays attention.

practice: Think of a living thing you pass all the time without knowing its name: the tree outside your window, the weed in the sidewalk crack, the small brown bird on the wire.
Picture its shape, its color, where it lives, and give it a few breaths of real attention. If you pray, you can give thanks for it.
